acceptance: Every issue the controller opens or reopens (refresh outcome and drift) reaches the owner through the route the owner chose, shown on a real or dry-run-equivalent issue.
The route is applied by the publish job, so the prepare job stays read-only and the write-confinement contract test passes unchanged.
downstream/MAINTAINING.md names who is expected to act on a controller issue, how they are notified and the expected response time before the next upstream tag.
context:
Decision gate: the owner chooses the route before any code changes, from (a) assign a named GitHub user on open; (b) apply a label the owner watches (for example benchbox-upstream) and subscribe to it; (c) also create or update a core tracker item when a drift or conflict issue opens; (d) document the red run as the only signal and accept the risk. Options can be combined. Record the choice in the context.

Verification rubric: (1) controller tests show the chosen assignee or label on upsert_issue and upsert_drift_issue operations; (2) the App's issue permissions cover the route (assigning needs no extra scope; labels must exist or be created by the publisher); (3) readiness still passes with the App's current permissions, or the permission change is approved and readiness updated; (4) after merge, the next issue the controller opens shows the route.

Guardrails: no new write permission in prepare or readiness; no App permission beyond issues:write without owner approval (readiness refuses excess permissions); do not post comments on every run, only on open or key change, to keep the first-red rule's noise level; no cross-repository writes unless the owner chose option (c).
